html:
A significant military escalation unfolded today as US forces conducted strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, marking the first known American attack on Iran since late July. Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps confirmed casualties, including civilians and fighters, and vowed retaliation, as the US stated its action was a response to IRGC forces preparing to launch sea mines into the critical Strait of Hormuz.

US Foreign Policy & Great Powers: Beyond the direct confrontation with Iran, US policy decisions and ongoing international disputes are prominent. Donald Trump announced a deal for a major US stake in Venezuelan oil reserves, with the administration stating it will soon begin refilling petroleum reserves using this oil, though energy experts express doubts. The diplomatic spat between the US and Canada over the administrative renaming of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" continues, with Canada erecting a defiant "Lake Ontario. Now and Always" sign as Google reportedly renames the lake for US users as Trump demanded. This conflict is tied to an escalating trade dispute. Meanwhile, Russia claimed it helped repel an attempted coup in Niger, and announced it is preparing "massive strikes" on Ukraine's energy sector.

Middle East Dynamics: The broader Middle East remains volatile amidst the US-Iran tension. Iran's supreme leader, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, called for Muslim unity against the US and Israel. In the Israeli-Palestinian context, Netanyahu vowed to establish more illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, while South Africa submitted a dossier to the International Court of Justice concerning Israel's non-compliance with provisional measures. Israeli forces bulldozed Palestinian land in Deir Ballut and conducted drone strikes in Gaza City, contributing to a reported Gaza death toll of 73,454. A far-right Israeli minister reportedly boasted about implementing worse prison conditions for Palestinian prisoners. Discussions are also underway regarding the future of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon, with Washington opposing its extension.

Global Disasters & Security: Humanitarian crises and security incidents captured global attention. Devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet have resulted in a death toll nearing 810, with over 3,000 people still missing, and authorities warning of possible fresh flooding as aid efforts continue. Separately, off northern Cyprus, a ferry carrying nearly 270 people capsized, killing at least eight and leaving others missing, leading to the arrest of the captain and crew. In Switzerland, a woman was killed and five others injured in a shooting at a techno event near Zurich, prompting a manhunt with police stating a terror motive is possible.

Domestic Politics & Governance: Political developments also made headlines globally. Zambian opposition leader Mundubile was charged with treason after reportedly seeking refuge in a United Nations building. Iceland rejected resuming membership talks with the European Union in a referendum held under the shadow of Trump’s threats regarding Greenland. In France, opinion polls for the next presidential election are predicting a victory for Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally. Donald Trump also threatened to report NBC anchor Kristen Welker to the Federal Communications Commission for "punishment" over her reporting on his endorsement results.

Science, Technology, and Social Impact: In a scientific milestone, NASA successfully launched a powerful new space telescope, starting a multi-year mission to map the universe and learn more about dark energy and dark matter. On the corporate front, Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement with multiple states over its platforms' contribution to a youth mental health crisis, hailed by regulators as a landmark moment.
